_comment: The viability run: one 4 h A100 run (spec section 8, run sheet D19-D52). Paths are relative to the repo root; every key can be overridden with --set a.b=value (scripts/04_distill.py). vast/bootstrap.sh reads sources, eval_sets, teacher_root, second_root, data_root, selection and student from this file. The differences from the DEFAULTS in scripts/04_distill.py: early_stop is on, and the eval cadence (eval.full_every_epochs, eval.mini, eval.probe_greedy_audio_s). EVALS: a FULL eval at the end of every epoch (eval.full_every_epochs 1; an epoch = one pass over the kept train rows, 233,094 utterances / 469 h = ~1,126 steps of 1500 audio-s): teacher-forced and greedy on the COMPLETE eval sets (16,240 utterances, 24.6 h; the gate sets JSUT / CV8 / ReazonSpeech-test are 14,746 and 21.9 h of them) plus the probe (teacher-forced on its 1,500 rows, greedy on a seeded ~600 s of it for the train CER). eval.every_min 20 is only the fallback cadence for full_every_epochs null (then an eval every 20 min of loop clock, greedy on the 500-per-set subset). A MINI eval every 200 optimizer steps, never at a full-eval step: 32 seeded utterances of each gate set + 64 of the probe, teacher-forced and greedy (~16 min of audio), logged under eval/mini/ and never used by the early stop or the verdict. Every eval logs its headline numbers under summary/full/ or summary/mini/ (val CER vs the reference and vs the teacher pooled over the gate sets, train CER, val / train KL and top-1) and prints one line. COST, AN ESTIMATE (no A100 measurement yet): the laptop's greedy decode of the 0.6B student measured RTF 0.048 (overfit-10s-20260924T095933Z, 2-utterance batches); scaled by the peak-FLOPS ratio 312/165 = 1.9 that is RTF ~0.026 on the A100, i.e. ~38 min of greedy decode per full eval (~34 min for the gate sets alone; the teacher-forced passes are ~15-30 s by FLOPs). One epoch is ~47 min at the smoke floor of 600 audio-s/s and ~10-13 min at 30-40 % MFU, so a full eval every epoch adds ~80 % (slow) to ~380 % (fast) of an epoch's training time, far above 20 %, and leaves room for only ~2-5 epoch-end evals in the 4 h (the early stop below needs at least 3 plus its patience). Decoding in large batches is much cheaper than those 2-utterance batches: at the teacher pass's batched laptop RTF (0.006-0.008, for the 2B teacher) a full eval is ~5-6 min, still ~10-60 % of an epoch. A mini eval costs ~25 s (tiny-batch scaling) or ~4 s (batched) per 200 steps (~2-8 min of training). The early stop: when the gate sets' pooled held-out KL (the verdict's) has not improved by 0.5 % relative for 3 in-loop (epoch-end) evals in a row (never before the 3rd eval after step 0), the WSD cooldown starts at once over 20 % of the loop time done so far (capped by the budget) and the run ends when it is over, instead of training on at a flat loss until the scheduled cooldown; already in the cooldown, the run goes on to its end. To stop by hand: touch runs/<run_id>/STOP (the end phase follows the step under way).
